content: The Great American Smokeout is an event aimed at encouraging individuals to quit smoking tobacco. It was first initiated in 1977 and is sponsored by the American Cancer Society. The event's spokesperson is Smokey Robinson. Participants are challenged to abstain from smoking cigarettes for a full 24 hours, with the hope that this temporary cessation will lead to a permanent commitment to quit smoking. The event takes place annually on the third Thursday of November, which is one week before Thanksgiving. In 2007, the 31st Great American Smokeout was scheduled for November 15. The event has its origins in a series of earlier initiatives. In 1971, Arthur P. Mullaney, in Randolph, Massachusetts, proposed that people refrain from smoking for a day and instead donate the money they would have spent on cigarettes to a local high school. Later, in 1974, Lynn R. Smith of the Monticello Times in Monticello, Minnesota, promoted a similar concept called Don't Smoke Day, also referred to as D-Day.
